_note: Written by tools/research.mjs and verified by tools/check-evidence.mjs. Every external figure's excerpt was found in its archived document and carries its value. Figures are the only numbers the writer may use.
title_idea: EU FDI screening notifications jumped 40% in 2025, and 12% of deals now face in-depth review
keyword: EU FDI screening notification 2025 in-depth assessment importer investor
angle: An importer or investor planning an EU acquisition or greenfield stake should budget for a 15-day notification window and a 12% chance of an in-depth security review, with the new FISR regime applying from 17 January 2028.

figures.unit: increase in notifications to the EU cooperation mechanism between 2024 and 2025
figures.source: European Commission, sixth annual FDI screening report
figures.evidence: the number of notifications to the EU’s cooperation mechanism increased by 40% between 2024 and 2025

figures.unit: investments notified to the Commission in 2025
figures.source: European Commission, sixth annual FDI screening report
figures.evidence: In 2025, EU Member States notified 667 investments to the Commission, up from 477 notifications in 2024.

figures.unit: investments notified to the Commission in 2024
figures.source: European Commission, sixth annual FDI screening report

figures.unit: share of notified cases closed within 15 days
figures.source: European Commission, sixth annual FDI screening report
figures.evidence: Of the 667 cases notified, 88% were closed within 15 days.

figures.unit: share of notified investments requiring an in-depth security risk assessment
figures.source: European Commission, sixth annual FDI screening report
figures.evidence: 12% of the investments notified to the Commission required an in-depth security risk assessment – a 4% rise compared to last year.

figures.unit: share of in-depth assessments in manufacturing
figures.source: European Commission, sixth annual FDI screening report
figures.evidence: Most such cases were in manufacturing, which accounted for 53% of all transactions (up from 50% in 2024).

figures.unit: date the new Foreign Investment Screening Regulation applies from
figures.source: European Commission, Foreign Investment Screening Regulation (FISR)
figures.evidence: The EU’s new Foreign Investment Screening Regulation (FISR) was adopted on 17 June 2026 and will apply from 17 January 2028.

sources: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security — 'Screening of foreign direct investment continues to advance EU security and public order', 14 October 2026
